checks: At each interior differentiability point the supporting tangent gives r−zr′≥r(0)>0. Local Lipschitz bounds and this lower derivative bound give a bi-Lipschitz change on every interior compact interval. A finite concave profile is bounded above by a supporting affine function and bounded away from zero by its endpoint chord. Interior exhaustion suffices even when an endpoint value differs from its interior limit.

Computing the inverse derivative gives dz/du=r²/(r−zr′), R′=−r′/(r−zr′) and R−uR′=1/(r−zr′). With d=m+1 the measure r^m dz is therefore exactly w(u)du, and wR has finite integral as the transformed r^(m−1) dz.

For s>0 the section is x=−z/s. Its graph length divided by √(1+s²) gives dz/s, so C and M have the stated raw rather than unit-normal section factors. Multiplication by z=u/R turns the C integrand into u w for M.

The captured fraction is zero below −s, one above s and (1+u/s)/2 between. Thus both saturated tails are retained and subtracting M gives the signed tail difference. On compact slope intervals away from zero the clipped fraction is uniformly Lipschitz. Its derivative off u=±s is −u/(2s²) on the active part and zero elsewhere. The threshold equalities are null for the w-density, so integrating proves the derivative relation.

Compared 5b3b585d1663ccd0 §4, (3)–(6), and 9cc7f272d6dd1c14 §§1–2, (1)–(6). The frozen proof rederives the chart under weaker regularity, then keeps the interval-layer normalization and both original saturated tails.

overlap.comparison: Gives the same projective chart and coarea coordinate on a C² or finite piecewise-affine homothetic body, in arbitrary horizontal dimension. This result weakens profile regularity for the interval-layer record and explicitly adds two saturated tails and the slope derivative.
Gives the unprojectivized raw coarea and vertical moment of the interval layers. It does not supply the projective two-tail formulas or the slope derivative.
Provides records on a particular decreasing affine frustum. That scope does not establish the displayed identities for general concave profiles.

readability: The density extensions outside the open chart apply to w and wR as products, so no reciprocal profile is evaluated there.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The reciprocal axial chart, the clipped cap fraction and the raw section integrals prove the two-tail formula and its slope derivative for arbitrary finite positive concave profiles.
